- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.4) within 3–5 days, model overreacts with downward bias; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.4) and price is trending downward; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; apply 2-period lag correction: if 2nd day of forecast is > 80, reduce by 0.5–1.5% for 3rd day.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.6), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 days for smoothing.
